name: Solvang Expedition Parka
description:
A knee-length expedition parka in deep forest green with a coyote-fur-trimmed hood — the fur is geneware-sourced, but the texture is indistinguishable from wild-caught. The outer shell is a heavyweight waxed cotton canvas that stiffens in cold but breaks in over time. Insulation is 800-fill down in a baffle construction that prevents cold spots. Storm placket over the main zip. Dual-entry hand pockets, two chest pockets, one interior security pocket. The wrist cuffs have internal knit draft stoppers.

Solvang is a Norwegian-heritage brand manufacturing in the Milwaukee district, and the parka is their flagship. No electronics, no smart fabric — just a coat built for the brutal stretch of January through March when the lake effect hits and the temperature drops to ranges that make outdoor activity genuinely dangerous. Tier 4 buyers own this as their serious cold-weather piece. The occasional Tier 2 worker saves for a year to buy one instead of buying three cheap coats that won't last.
what_it_says: You've invested in something built to last because you understand the difference between cost and value. You have probably been very cold before and decided never again.
worn_by: architects and engineers doing site work
anyone who commutes on foot through a GLMZ winter
story_hooks: Solvang's geneware fur supplier was just raided by a corponation claiming IP theft on the fur-gene sequence — the brand's next production run is in legal limbo
A Solvang parka was found floating in the lake near the port district, still buttoned, no identification inside — and the water in the interior pockets was fresh, not salt
Someone has been leaving Solvang parkas in Tier 1 drop points — anonymous, no note, always in the right size for the person who finds them

physical_description.visual_profile: A substantial, structured knee-length silhouette with pronounced shoulders. The deep forest green creates an authoritative presence against urban concrete. The coyote-fur hood trim frames the face with luxurious fullness, contrasting sharply against the utilitarian canvas body. Reads as serious, capable, built for survival rather than aesthetics.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with enough room for layering beneath. Slightly tapered at the waist to prevent bulk. Sleeves cut long enough to cover wrist augmentation ports. Hood designed to accommodate various head shapes and internal tech without compression.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight waxed cotton canvas — industrial-grade, naturally water-resistant, develops a patina with use. Geneware coyote fur trim (ethically sourced, lab-grown to spec). 800-fill down insulation in baffle-box construction.
physical_description.texture: Canvas is stiff when new, with a subtle waxy sheen that dulls with wear. Develops creases and soft folds over time. Fur is dense and tactile, shedding-resistant. Interior knit cuffs are soft against skin. Brass hardware ages to a warm patina.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep forest green (primary) — a shade chosen for visibility in whiteout conditions and absence of corpo branding colors. Coyote fur trim in warm tan-gray. Brass zippers and toggle buttons add warm metallic notes. Interior lining is neutral charcoal.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty brass YKK zipper with storm placket overlay. Four brass toggle buttons at chest. Brass buckles on side vents for adjustability. Wrist cuffs have internal elastic with knit draft stoppers — no external closure needed.
distinctive_features: Storm placket prevents wind infiltration along main zipper
Dual-entry hand pockets cut deep for extended glove wear
Two chest pockets (one accessible, one internal security pocket for valuables)
Internal security pocket positioned at sternum for documents or currency chips
Geneware fur trim indistinguishable from wild-caught — ethical sourcing without compromise
Baffle-box down construction eliminates cold spots and maintains loft
Vents at side seams with adjustable buckles for temperature regulation
Reinforced stress points at shoulders, underarms, and pocket entries
No integrated tech — pure analog, fully repairable
Solvang woven label at interior collar (understated branding)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 primary market (working-class professionals, skilled labor, independent contractors). Occasional Tier 2 purchase (corporate workers saving for quality). Resale value strong — secondhand Solvang parkas common in Tier 4-5 markets.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals practical competence, preparedness, and connection to pre-digital manufacturing values. Worn by maintenance workers, logistics coordinators, outdoor researchers, and anyone who takes winter survival seriously. Absence of tech or augmentation-specific features reads as 'I don't need smart to stay alive.' Milwaukee heritage and Norwegian ancestry appeal to working-class diaspora communities in GLMZ.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, but quickly develops character — canvas creases follow the wearer's posture, fur loses initial fluffiness, brass develops patina. Typical worn example shows scuff marks at cuff edges, slight graying of canvas where hands frequently contact, and broken-in collar that molds to neck shape. This wear is considered desirable; it proves functionality.
